findings.reason: the plan should extend one unit renderer (the owner in reckon/service.py) with the watcher's extra Environment line, which deletes the duplicate and makes the parity test unnecessary instead of codifying it.
findings.text: WATCH_UNIT_TEMPLATE restates the whole [Service] body of reckon/service.py:24 UNIT_TEMPLATE (same ExecStart/StandardOutput/StandardError/Restart/RestartSec/TimeoutStopSec skeleton), and §9's design deliberately kept both copies, changed Restart in each, and pinned them with a cross-copy parity assertion rather than unifying them, so the restart policy and the unit body still have two homes a future edit can desynchronize — exactly the two-readers-defect this plan removes everywhere else

findings.reason: the two answer different questions (the launcher's selected origin, probed over HTTP, versus the endpoints a lane publishes), the plan documented the distinction as prior art before the node ran, and folding them would destroy the launcher-origin signal the section exists to add.
findings.text: a second backend-reachability verdict ("status"/"serving") sits beside reckon/flight.py::_probe_serving, which already returns serving/serving_detail for a backend

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the one new module, reckon/crew/serving_origin.py, hides origin discovery and a bounded HTTP probe behind a single callable check_serving_origin, and every other section extends an existing reader (recovery, promotion, dispatch, runs) rather than adding surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the systemd unit renderer is duplicated between reckon/service.py:24 (UNIT_TEMPLATE) and reckon/crew/runs.py:3320 (WATCH_UNIT_TEMPLATE); §9 patched both copies and added a parity test instead of extending one owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebases it extends and cites the mechanism each section reuses: reckon/flight.py::_probe_serving and endpoints_document for §13, the mounted-project map plus repository_identity for §6, watcher_state for §3, the existing no-op-probe reader in reckon/crew/recovery.py for §4, and _live_pointer_worktrees for §44–§47.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §13 states why reckon/flight.py's endpoints reader cannot answer which origin a resolved launcher selects, so the new callable is not a thin layer over machinery that could simply be extended.
